entries: Content preparation and sequencing | Decide the content before going on mic | Research background materials to prepare programs and interviews, write and edit scripts and video scripts, select program content with producers based on program positioning and audience tastes, develop storylines, and maintain the music library.

On-air presentation and links | Deliver consistently and control duration | Read news bulletins, identify the station and open or close programs (improvising or using memorized material and scripts), announce and comment on music, weather, and traffic, send network cue signals, and control segment lengths according to time slots.

Interviews and conversations | Present guests clearly | Interview guests about their experiences, work, or current affairs, find and confirm guests, host panel discussions and talk programs, and communicate with listeners or viewers by telephone when necessary.

Live events and promotion | Represent the institution | Provide commentary and interviews at sporting events, parades, and conferences, host public-interest and promotional events, attend press conferences to gather information, and represent the employer at public or private events.

Technical operation and recording | Ensure broadcast readiness | Operate consoles, play and sequence music selections, advertisements, and public-service messages, and record advertisements for later broadcast; specific production/technical collaboration is an editorial question to verify for the role.

Records and archiving | Make broadcasts traceable | Keep daily program logs recording elements such as the day’s broadcast music selections and station promotions, and organize and maintain materials and music libraries; incident reporting and recording procedures are editorial questions to verify with the actual institution.

entries.answer: Broadcast announcers and radio DJs correspond to the US occupation Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys (27-3011.00). They read scripts such as news and commercial messages, play/sequence music, identify the station, and interview guests. ONET lists 24 tasks: 19 core and 5 supplemental, including background research, news rewriting, script editing, console operation, advertisement recording, program logs, content selection, sports commentary, and music library maintenance; a particular position need not perform all of them. The related Chinese occupational category is announcers and program hosts (2-10-04), which does not correspond one-to-one to every event hosting or voice-over position.

subject.name: Broadcast Announcers and Radio DJs
subject.summary: Broadcast announcers and radio DJs correspond to the US occupation Broadcast Announcers and Radio Disc Jockeys (27-3011.00). They read scripts such as news and commercial messages, play/sequence music, identify the station, and interview guests. ONET lists 24 tasks: 19 core and 5 supplemental, including background research, news rewriting, script editing, console operation, advertisement recording, program logs, content selection, sports commentary, and music library maintenance; a particular position need not perform all of them. The related Chinese occupational category is announcers and program hosts (2-10-04), which does not correspond one-to-one to every event hosting or voice-over position. The US May2025 median annual wage is USD 47,340. BLS EP 27-3011: 21,800 people in 2025, 20,200 in 2035, a decline of 7.6% over 2025–2035, an official net decrease of 1,700 people, 2,000 annual average job openings, and 2.3% self-employed. Employment figures are rounded; the net decrease uses the official tabulated value. Openings include replacement needs and do not equal net new jobs or an individual’s chance of being hired.
